description:
Share expensive immutable profile and derived-state setup across test processes while preserving isolated mutable repositories and the full-stack interfaces each test proves.

## Background

The warm profile shows profile lifecycle, derived-state repair, and related in-crate profile/init/validate tests dominate the reducible aggregate suite work. Many tests independently construct equivalent dogfood packages and repository baselines before applying a small scenario-specific mutation. Cache only verified immutable inputs or baselines keyed by every source and binary input that affects them, then create a cheap isolated copy for each test before mutation.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Repeated profile and derived-state repair tests reuse verified immutable package or repository baselines and create isolated mutable state per test, eliminating equivalent full setup work across nextest processes.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every existing stable test identity and semantic assertion remains, including full CLI/process boundaries where those are the property under test; no assertion is replaced with a mocked or lower-layer surrogate.
- [hard] REQ-03: Cache keys cover source, profile assets, executable provenance, and setup shape; publication is atomic, concurrent, fail-closed on corruption or occupied destinations, and never exposes or reuses mutable repository state.
- [hard] REQ-04: Focused profile, init, validate, derived-state repair, and fixture-integrity tests pass together with the cargo-ci self-test, formatting, and warning-free linting; the integrated parent profile demonstrates the final aggregate reduction.

## Notes

Expected test-only support is in `crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs` and existing shared harness support, consumed by profile CLI/acceptance, derived-state repair, and in-crate init/profile/validate tests only where profiling proves equivalent setup. Production transaction behavior is out of scope. Do not regenerate the integrated suite profile in this leaf.
title: Share immutable profile and repair fixtures across nextest processes
